summary: The article accurately explains the difference between direct and regular mutual funds and the recent SEBI mandate. The claims are well-supported by authoritative sources.

claims.claim: SEBI has mandated that online execution-only platforms must offer direct plans as the default option for mutual fund transactions.
claims.note: SEBI mandated that direct plans be the default option on AMC digital platforms from November 1, 2026.

claims.claim: If a regular plan has an expense ratio of 1.5% per annum, its direct counterpart might have an expense ratio of 0.75% to 1% per annum. While this difference might seem small, perhaps 0.5% to 0.75% annually, its compounding effect over decades can be substantial.
claims.note: Regular plans have a higher expense ratio due to distributor commissions, typically ranging from 0.5% to 1.5% higher than direct plans.

claims.claim: Direct plans are designed for investors who are comfortable doing their own research, making their own investment decisions, and managing their own portfolios. These plans can be purchased directly from the Asset Management Companies (AMCs) or through online platforms that offer execution-only services.
claims.note: Direct plans are for investors who invest directly with AMCs without intermediaries, often through AMC websites or execution-only platforms.

claims.claim: The Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) website (https://amfiindia.com)
claims.note: The AMFI website is correctly cited.

claims.claim: You can find the expense ratio for any mutual fund scheme on the respective Asset Management Company's (AMC) website, on the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) website (https://amfiindia.com), or in the scheme's offer document.
claims.note: Expense ratios are disclosed on AMC websites and the AMFI website.

claims.claim: SEBI's new rule is a step towards greater transparency in mutual fund investing. By making direct plans the default, it forces investors to acknowledge the cost difference and make an informed choice.
claims.note: SEBI's mandate aims to improve transparency and investor awareness regarding the cost difference between direct and regular plans.

article_title: Direct vs. Regular Mutual Funds: SEBI's New Default Plan Rule
